transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-09-11 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (NorthStar Platform), Diego Ramos (NorthStar CTO), Priya Singh (NorthStar DevOps), Liam Ortiz (NorthStar SRE)

Summary note: informal walkthrough, many live code references. Transcript has minor transcription errors (proper nouns sometimes off).

00:00 - Samira Patel: Hey everyone, welcome, thanks for making time. quick intros — I'm Samira, AE at Redwood, and with me is Ethan our SE, he'll walk through the SDK and a couple of live snippets.
00:14 - Maya Chen: hi, thanks, we got a couple of questions up front around auth and our SSO integration, also curious about how the env setup looks in our CI.
00:22 - Samira Patel: perfect, that'll be in the agenda, we want to show both python and typescript quickstarts, and then the console bits for Optimize and monitoring.
00:35 - Ethan Cole: cool, i'll start with a tiny python example, sorry if my mic bumps — so pip install redwood-inference-sdk, that's the CLI/pkg name we expose, or npm i @redwood/inference for node.
00:49 - Diego Ramos: wait are those the exact package names? i saw different names in the docs, was there a legacy package?
00:55 - Ethan Cole: yeah there's historical naming, the canonical repos are linked in the quickstart we will share, but the main published packages are redwood-inference-sdk and @redwood/inference, we keep both maintained.
01:08 - Priya Singh: for auth, we use SSO with Okta, we can't put long-lived keys in code. what are the SSO options?
01:15 - Samira Patel: good point — we support API keys for quickstart and CI, and for enterprise we do SAML/SSO integration with short-lived tokens and on-prem private control plane. you can also integrate with your KMS for key rotation.
01:29 - Ethan Cole: to add, we offer a SAML flow that issues ephemeral credentials to your app, and for CI/CD we recommend using environment variables sourced from your vault (Hashi, AWS Secrets Manager) rather than embedding in repos.
01:42 - Maya Chen: ok, show us the code pattern — node and python examples for fetching ephemeral tokens or using env var?
01:48 - Ethan Cole: sure — python snippet: from redwood import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')); resp = client.generate("hello world") — simple. for ephemeral SSO we provide an auth proxy and an OIDC flow; the SDK accepts a token string same as api_key param.
02:07 - Liam Ortiz: do you recommend separate service accounts per environment? staging vs prod?
02:12 - Samira Patel: yes, separate service accounts + RBAC is best practice, we expose token scopes so you can limit to embeddings only or generation only.
02:22 - Diego Ramos: about env setup in pipelines — we run GitHub Actions and GitLab CI; any gotchas?
02:28 - Ethan Cole: main gotcha is to not leak token in logs; use secrets masking and the SDK has a verbose mode you should avoid in public logs. We'll include example GitHub Action steps in the repo.
02:40 - Maya Chen: what's the recommended node runtime for @redwood/inference? we use node 18.
02:44 - Ethan Cole: node 18+ is fine, we test 18 and 20. typescript typings are published with the package.
03:00 - Samira Patel: switching topics — Optimize recommendations: Ethan can show an example where we suggest batch size and quantization profile based on traffic pattern.
03:10 - Ethan Cole: yeah, Optimize gives suggestions; for chat workloads we often recommend small batching with prefix caching. you'll see recommendations like "batch 8, kv cache enabled, use int8 qprofile-a" — note sometimes the tool mislabels q-profiles in the UI as qprof-1, that's a naming nit.
03:30 - Priya Singh: our compliance team will want SOC2 docs and proof of key management. do you support HSM-backed KMS?
03:36 - Samira Patel: we integrate with customer-managed KMS keys for Private deployments and we support HSM-backed providers via KMS integrations; hosted customers can use our managed keys but enterprise can bring their own. we'll send the SOC2 and KMS checklist.
03:52 - Diego Ramos: latency — we need 95th p95 < 200ms for our short prompts, is that realistic on hosted?
03:59 - Ethan Cole: depends on model and sequence length; small open models on dedicated capacity can hit that, hosted API typically 100–400ms for short prompts depending on region. if you need strict SLOs, Dedicated is the usual path. We can run a quick benchmark during POC.
04:18 - Maya Chen: can the SDK stream tokens in node as server-sent events or do we have to poll?
04:24 - Ethan Cole: we support streaming over websocket and event-stream in node; python has streaming iterators. quick code: client.stream_generate(...). On the node side we also have an example using fetch + ReadableStream.
04:40 - Priya Singh: are there any sandbox limits we should know for trial org?
04:44 - Samira Patel: trial orgs get limited quotas but enough for a POC; we'll outline quotas in the onboarding email.
04:52 - Diego Ramos: we run models in a VPC for data residency — if we go private, how hard is network setup?
04:58 - Ethan Cole: for Redwood Private we provide a control plane and you deploy agents in your VPC. network-wise it's typical VPN or private peering; some teams do an air-gapped install. Ethan: (laughs) there's a checklist.
05:15 - Liam Ortiz: what logs do we get? can we ship them to Splunk or S3?
05:19 - Samira Patel: yes, audit logs, request/response traces (configurable retention) can be exported to S3, GCS, or SIEMs like Splunk. we'll share the logging export doc.
05:30 - Maya Chen: can you show the quickstart repo layout?
05:33 - Ethan Cole: sure, i shared my screen — repo root has /python, /node, /benchmarks, /demo-config. Python quickstart has install, env.example, and simple generate.py. Node quickstart has example TS and JS.
05:50 - Ethan Cole: live code: generate.py snippet prints token counts and latency. note sometimes the transcript uses marching numbers by mistake, you'll see 'KV cash' in some older notes, meant 'KV cache'.
06:10 - Diego Ramos: what's the recommended pattern for secret rotation in CI?
06:14 - Ethan Cole: short-lived tokens with role-based rotation. If you're using GitHub Actions, inject via OIDC to AWS STS and fetch secret from Secrets Manager at runtime.
06:28 - Maya Chen: internal question: can we pin a model version to avoid drift during rollout?
06:32 - Samira Patel: yes, the API allows model pinning and rollout policies. you can do canary traffic split and fallback rules.
06:42 - Priya Singh: about billing — do you provide per-route breakdowns? we need token-level cost attribution for different teams.
06:46 - Samira Patel: Console shows token breakdown by API key and route, and you can export CSV for internal allocation.
06:55 - Diego Ramos: are there SDK-specific rate limits?
06:58 - Ethan Cole: limits are per account; the SDK doesn't enforce additional limits but will surface 429s and backoff headers. we include an exponential backoff helper.
07:12 - Maya Chen: for the POC, we expect to test both hosted and dedicated quickly. timeline?
07:17 - Samira Patel: proposed: kickoff 2025-09-18, 2-week hosted performance test, then evaluate Dedicated/Private decision. total POC 4 weeks.
07:30 - Diego Ramos: stakeholder check: our security reviewer (Priya) will need SOC2 and encryption flow, and Liam will run the SRE tests.
07:38 - Priya Singh: yes, and we need to confirm data-retention defaults and deletion API.
07:42 - Ethan Cole: deletion API exists for hosted and private, with configurable retention. we'll include endpoints in the doc.
07:52 - Samira Patel: any blockers on your side for the kickoff?
07:55 - Maya Chen: only approvals from legal, should be ok early next week.
08:00 - Diego Ramos: competition question — we've looked at Anthropic and Vertex — what's the differentiator?
08:06 - Samira Patel: our differentiator is inference economics and production features: caching, smart batching, and unified tooling across hosted/dedicated/private; we provide actionable Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization, and clear SLOs.
08:20 - Ethan Cole: also our runtime has kernel selection for different GPUs which often helps with latency; that detail tends to matter in heavy loads.
08:30 - Maya Chen: ok, show me the sample benchmark script.
08:33 - Ethan Cole: in /benchmarks we have node_bench.js which hits the API with a mix of prompt lengths and records p50/p95/p99. it's deliberately small so you can run locally or in CI.
08:50 - Priya Singh: can we run it from our VPC to test egress and latency?
08:54 - Ethan Cole: yes for Private you run agents inside your VPC, for hosted you can run the script from your network to measure real egress times. we'll provide a runbook.
09:05 - Diego Ramos: any special CSPM or infra checks for private install?
09:10 - Samira Patel: our private install docs include network, IAM, and minimal required ports; some teams have to open specific outbound ports for the control plane, we'll share the network diagram.
09:22 - Maya Chen: quick question about embeddings local cache — do we store embedding vectors in our DB or do you offer a managed vector DB?
09:27 - Ethan Cole: Redwood doesn't host a managed vector DB by default; we recommend storing vectors in your vector store (Pinecone, Milvus, or internal store). we do offer an optional embedding cache to reduce repeat calls.
09:40 - Liam Ortiz: what's the expected tokens per second throughput for a 4-GPU dedicated pool?
09:44 - Ethan Cole: depends on model and sequence length; roughly for a medium open model you might see 200–400 tps per GPU with batching. we'll include more exact numbers in the benchmark sheet.
09:56 - Samira Patel: ok wrapping up, let's recap next steps and owners.
10:02 - Samira Patel: recap: Samira will send quickstart repo and onboarding steps; Ethan sends benchmark scripts and runbook; customer to confirm stakeholders and legal, then kickoff week of 9/18.
10:14 - Maya Chen: sounds good, thanks everyone.
10:18 - Diego Ramos: thank you, excited to test.
10:22 - Priya Singh: thanks, talk soon.
10:26 - Samira Patel: i'll follow up with calendar invite for kickoff and the docs.

End of transcript (minor transcription noise and mislabels present).
